subject: performance question / managing the AD stack

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: performance question / managing the AD stack
parts:
Hi!

Managing the AD stack size is always critical in Stan applications as I am aware, but is it about sheer size or about values ever calculated?

So what I am doing is to calculate concentrations at different time-points in a multi-compartement system which are subject to dosing.

Say I have D = 10 dosing events and T = 100 time-points in a system with C=3 compartements. The data at hand is always observing only a single c_obs compartment out of the three. At the moment my Stan program will calculate a T * C matrix, then subset to the column c_obs of the matrix which I have observed. Therefore, I only need T variables out of the T*C.

My question now - is this inefficient? As alternative I could move C states from the first to the last time-point and along the way output the T states of the observed compartement.

So is it very costly to have many temporary AD variables around or should I try to avoid these?

Thanks much.

Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] performance question / managing the AD stack
parts:
Operations add about 40 bytes to the stack. And
each one adds a run-time virtual funcition call and
sometimes non-memory-local pointer chasing.

Our matrix operations try to be conservative with
memory, so there will be a breakeven point where doing
it by hand will be faster.

The arXiv paper goes into more detail.

- Bob
